title: NATO secretary general confirms North Korean troops deployed to Russia's Kursk region
body:
On 28 October 2024 NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte confirmed that North Korean troops had been deployed to Russia's Kursk region, as reported by Reuters and relayed by Novaya Gazeta Europe. Rutte said the deployment showed Vladimir Putin's growing desperation and that Putin was unable to sustain his assault on Ukraine without foreign support. He also said that over 600,000 Russian soldiers had been killed or wounded.

Ukraine's military intelligence chief, Kyrylo Budanov, had said that 11,000 North Korean infantry troops were training in Russia's Far East and that the first contingent was due in Kursk the previous Wednesday. South Korean intelligence had earlier reported that Pyongyang planned to send about 12,000 troops. Andriy Yermak, chief of staff to President Zelensky, said North Korean troops were already in Kursk and urged allies to supply weapons and a clear plan.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the reports conflicting. At the BRICS summit in Kazan, Putin did not deny that North Korean soldiers were being trained to fight in Ukraine, and cited a mutual defence clause in the Russia-North Korea pact, which the Russian parliament had ratified shortly before.
